Column definitions

Breakdown

GroupHiresTo hireTo offerConfidence
Method

Candidates hired in the last 90 days, grouped by the selected dimension. To hire is that group's average residency summed across every stage from Submitted through Offer, plus Offer itself; to offer is the same sum without the Offer-stage residency. Because this is restricted to the same completed cohort at every stage, the sum reflects real elapsed time rather than mixing populations with different denominators. Under 6 hires is too small and directional only.

Workday Q4 Median Time to Fill

RecruiterMedian days to fillFills
Source

Workday Time to Offer (Jul 2025 – Aug 2026)

Real Workday time-to-offer data, one row per hire. Filterable by recruiter, hiring manager, or cost center — pick a group to see its aggregate average. A static extract — won't update until a new one is provided. Not the same window as the 90-day figures elsewhere on this dashboard, so the two aren't meant to reconcile.

RecruiterHiresMedian days to offerMean days to offer
RecruiterHiring managerCost centerMonthDays to offer
Method

From a Workday extract: Cost Center × Hiring Manager × Recruiter, with one days-to-offer figure per month, Jul 2025 onward only (excludes Apr–Jun 2025 present in the source file, per the user's instruction). Each non-zero monthly cell is treated as exactly one hire — no weighting or hire-count assumption beyond that. This is the correct, complete extract, superseding all prior partial pulls. Org-wide: 1,750 hires, median 34.5 days, mean 41.5 days. This dataset drives the org-wide Time to Offer header tile — median is shown there, since real outliers (a few reqs over 200 days) skew the mean upward.

Workday Time to Hire (Jul 2025 – Sep 2026)

Not the header's source. The header's Time to Hire (66d) is the prior validated full-cycle estimate, last checked Aug 4. This raw extract's own median (20.2d) and mean (28.0d) are skewed by a large number of fast internal hires/transfers (~3 days) that aren't representative of typical external hiring — shown below for reference, not driving the header.

RecruiterHiresMedian days to hireMean days to hire
Method

"Total Days to Hire" is Workday's own sum of days in Submitted + Screen + Interview + Offer + Hire stages, per filled requisition. Includes internal hires/transfers, which typically skip most stages and post near-zero day counts — this pulls both the median and mean down relative to a pure external-hire figure. This report only breaks down by Recruiter and Job Requisition, so no Hiring Manager or Cost Center view is available for this metric (unlike Time to Offer).

Days in stage, for candidates who moved

RecruiterSubmittedPre to active offer
Do not add these together

Per-stage residence times for candidates who exited the stage in the window. Summing them across stages produces a wrong total because each stage has a different denominator; most candidates skip at least one round. These compare a single step over time, not the full journey.

Method

Average days per stage — Q4 (Apr 6 – Jun 30, 2026)

Workday-sourced, weighted by candidate volume per requisition. A different period and source than the rest of this dashboard — not meant to reconcile with the 90-day figures above. Reflects role mix (technical reqs run longer than high-volume roles) more than individual pace — read directionally, not as a ranking.

RecruiterSubmittedScreenInterviewOfferTotal to hireCandidates
Method

From Workday's "Average Days Per Recruiting Stage" report, Apr 6 – Jun 30, 2026. Each recruiter's per-requisition stage averages are weighted by that requisition's candidate count and combined into one figure per stage. Only recruiters matching the current roster are shown (26 of 33 in the source file); 6 no longer track hires here and are omitted. The source file's own org-wide total: 26.4d Submitted, 13.3d Screen, 12.1d Interview, 3.0d Offer, 54.8d total.

Round-level Paradox usage

Real Gem stage-entry data on Round 1/2/3. Interview/Additional Interview (manual) and Round 1/2/3 PDX (automated) are parallel paths for the same step, not sequential — a recruiter uses one or the other per candidate. See the Screen 1 card below for the initial screen. Only counts candidates through a Workday-integrated PDX stage — if a recruiter uses the Paradox browser extension directly, it shows here as manual even though Paradox was used.

RecruiterManual InterviewPDX roundsTotal% via Paradox
Method

From Gem's stage-entry data: candidates entering the plain "Interview" stage vs. the "Round 1 PDX" / "Round 2 PDX" / "Round 3 PDX" stages.

Screen 1 Paradox usage

Real Gem stage-entry data on Screen 1. Gem separates the manual "Recruiter Screen" stage from the automated "Recruiter Screen PDX" stage — this is a direct split, not inferred. The main dashboard continues to show these combined as one "Screen" figure everywhere else. Only counts candidates through a Workday-integrated PDX stage — if a recruiter uses the Paradox browser extension directly, it shows here as manual even though Paradox was used.

RecruiterManual ScreenPDX ScreenTotal% via Paradox
Method

From Gem's stage-entry data: candidates entering "Recruiter Screen" (manual) vs. "Recruiter Screen PDX" (Paradox-scheduled — covers Screen 1, Screen 1 Phone PDX, Screen 1 Teams PDX, and Screen 1 Teams 45 PDX).
